conclusions: All 18 scenarios preserved the exact retained-root count and set hash across versions and states; no timing improvement is obtained by reducing frozen coverage.
SPI-PSS initial combined startup increased 361.767 to 431.729 ms; five crossover batches did not reproduce it: 360.257 to 359.897 ms. Both datasets are retained.

SoC full-lifecycle combined startup increased 5097.150 to 5488.862 ms in the main matrix, and 5147.357 to 5490.542 ms in two crossover batches. Startup-only readiness checks were 4961.903 to 4940.135 ms; no stable overall startup improvement is claimed.
Existing phase timers in separate readiness runs showed owner certification 1017.751 to 875.569 ms. Nested phases overlap and must not be summed or treated as qualified end-to-end latency.

SoC freeze-only main lifecycle peak increased 3258.441 to 3868.722 MiB, concentrated at manual rebuild. Crossover peaks varied for both versions, with compression in one run of each version. Final active allocator bytes differed by 3548016 bytes (3.384 MiB); peak footprint is not equated to retained live-object size.
The persistent index/snapshot additions are small in the measured workloads, but heavy-rebuild physical peaks and full-lifecycle startup remain variable; this change does not claim to improve them.
Typical existing-project first/continuous edit timings are largely unchanged. The demonstrated gains are selected-metadata scaling and reduced certification phase work.
